title: Verifier-Guided Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered Paired Study under Shared Initial Candidate Semantics
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) when the identical single initial generation is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we executed N=200 intent→configuration tasks with a hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (model configuration records temperature = null/unset). Provider-call reconciliation shows 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired contingency counts: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial two-sided convention) yields p = 1.0 for the observed discordant pair pattern (n = 1, k = 1). A paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute risk difference equals [0.00, 0.015]. Archived validator tracer fields show the single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step required_sequence ordering breach in a task labeled by the generator with difficulty metadata required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme". We provide the preregistration, full execution accounting, paired analysis, a localized failure diagnosis grounded in archived validator traces, and bounded operational interpretations tied to the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Translating high-level operator intent into device configurations is a growing application area for generative large language models (LLMs). Operational acceptance of generated configurations depends on satisfying deterministic invariants — e.g., required multi-step ordering, allowed field modifications, group-level availability constraints, and other workflow policies. Architectures that pair generation with deterministic verification and bounded automated repair are proposed to reduce hazardous misconfigurations, but the marginal effect of an automated repair step on an identical generated candidate is not generally quantified. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both conditions), any paired difference isolates only downstream validator-triggered repair effects; it does not capture gains that would arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, or multi-sample selection.

This study was preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed to estimate the repair-only marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair on LLM-generated network configurations. Our primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We emphasize that shared_initial_candidate semantics mean baseline and guarded episodes begin from exactly the same generated candidate; therefore, observed paired differences arise solely from deterministic validation and any permitted repair.
sections.related_work: Prior work demonstrates active development of intent→configuration systems and benchmark-style evaluations that motivate verifier-aware pipelines [1],[2],[?]. The supplied literature synthesis supports three claims: (i) intent→configuration pipelines are actively prototyped with benchmark evaluations and prototype systems [NetConfEval and others]; (ii) deterministic verifiers are an appropriate operational oracle for syntactic and semantic invariants in configuration-synthesis evaluation; and (iii) generate→validate→repair patterns and tool-augmented LLM agents are a recurring design motif in adjacent domains (program repair, model repair, and tool-augmented agents) but their measured effects in NetOps-specific, multi-device sequencing contexts remain an open empirical question. The present paired, shared_initial_candidate experiment addresses the narrower empirical gap of quantifying the marginal (repair-only) effect when identical initial candidates are reused across baseline and guarded conditions. Existing demonstrations in other domains motivate guarded pipelines but do not by themselves establish effectiveness for multi-device ordering or group-constraint faults in network configurations; our study contributes a tightly artifacted, verifier-backed measurement to that conversation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The experiment and analysis plan were frozen in preregistration CAND-2026-001 before any model calls. Key preregistered elements: paired binary estimand comparing per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance under baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator may invoke ≤1 automated repair) conditions; task_count = 200; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task reused by both episodes); deterministic task selection via the adapter’s fixed index rule; a maximum of one automated repair call per task; primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary; and confirmatory tests consisting of an exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial-tail convention) and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration artifact and execution manifest are archived in the run bundle.

Deterministic task generation and verifier oracle. Tasks originate from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with fixed generation seeds and per-task manifests that encode initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence ordering, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic oracle for this synthetic bank: it parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (e.g., final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and emits structured tracer outputs used for scoring. Per-episode scorer outputs are boolean (full_intent_constraint_validation true only when all encoded constraints are satisfied) and include rich validation_before/validation_after tracer fields archived for diagnostic analysis.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling notes. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the exact same initial generation (the single sampled candidate) was provided to both baseline and guarded episodes. Consequently, any observed paired difference is attributable only to deterministic validation and the single permitted repair; it cannot reflect prompt-template differences, multiple-sample selection, or independent guarded first-pass generations. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a background property even though the experiment reuses exactly one initial sample per pair by design.

Generation sanitizer and bounded repair policy. Each generated candidate passed through a deterministic formatting sanitizer before verification. If the verifier reported invariant violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model with a repair prompt constructed from the archived validator trace (pre-registered). Repairs were counted against the maximum_model_calls budget; deterministic reconciliation records shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1 (201 model calls total). Persistent unparsables after sanitizer and the allowed repair were handled according to the preregistered missingness plan; the primary analysis applied complete_pair_primary.

Provider-call accounting and reconciliation. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json record stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, and cache_hit_count = 0. These artifacts are the authoritative evidence for model-call accounting and show that the run used exactly one repair-stage call across all pairs.

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory test uses exact two-sided McNemar from discordant pair counts n10 and n01, computed with the exact-binomial-tail two-sided convention implemented in the archived analysis executor. For n = n10 + n01 and k = n10, p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} with the conventional handling when k = 0. For the paired absolute risk difference we computed a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; these parameters and seed are recorded in the archived analysis log. All code and parameters required to reproduce the analysis are included in the archived analysis executor.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The execution manifest records start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (elapsed ≈29 minutes). planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400 with failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call reconciliation reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0. The analysis executor reports complete_pairs = 200 with baseline_success_count = 199 and guarded_success_count = 200 (baseline success_rate = 0.995; guarded success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, yielding a paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Confirmatory inference and uncertainty. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the archived exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the absolute risk difference computed with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) equals [0.00, 0.015]. These numerical results and the analysis log are archived and reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the recorded raw results.

Single repair event and diagnostic trace. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator tracer outputs for the repaired pair indicate the shared initial candidate violated the task’s required_sequence ordering constraint; the task’s generator-assigned difficulty metadata for that repaired pair is recorded as required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme" in the task manifest. The validator trace records validation_before.violation_codes that indicate an ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied. In short, the archived evidence shows the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered bounded repair that corrected an ordering/dependency violation expressible in the task manifest’s invariants.

Missingness, exclusions, and deterministic reconciliation. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no persistent unparsables; missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros for other missingness categories. Deterministic reconciliation indicates pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. No episodes have terminal errors, and provider-call audit details align with preregistration.
sections.discussion:
Design rationale and interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics was chosen to measure the repair-only marginal effect: by deterministically reusing the identical initial generation for baseline and guarded episodes, differences can arise only from deterministic downstream validation and the single permitted repair. This narrow estimand isolates verifier-triggered correction capacity but does not address effects that could arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompts, or multi-sample selection; those contrasts are explicitly outside this experiment’s design scope.

Sparse-discordant regime and statistical limits. The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) placed the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime with only one discordant pair. Under the exact-binomial two-sided McNemar convention the observed discordant pattern yields p = 1.0, which reflects the small discordant-sample evidence available for directional inference rather than evidence that the guarded pipeline is ineffective. The paired-bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies plausible absolute improvements compatible with the data and bounds the repair-only effect; the upper CI bound indicates that, in this repair-only estimand and on this synthetic bank, an absolute guarded improvement larger than ~1.5 percentage points is not supported by the observed sample. The preregistered power rationale anticipated detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (baseline ~45–65%); unexpectedly high baseline performance therefore reduced realized inferential sensitivity for small marginal effects.

Failure-mode structure and difficulty stratification. Representative task manifests and archived validator tracers encode difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). In the archived representative subset required_command_count values span 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3; the lone baseline failure and the single repaired pair are associated with extreme composite difficulty patterns (highest required_command_count and multiple changed interfaces). This pattern is consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures and that bounded repair can address certain localized ordering/dependency violations that are expressible in the verifier’s invariants.

Operational implications and bounded claims. Artifact-grounded evidence supports only a narrow operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank evaluated by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and using the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized multi-step ordering fault in one extreme task. This is direct evidence that verifier-guided bounded repair can remedy certain ordering/dependency violations expressible in task manifests. It is not evidence that bounded repair will correct omissions observable only at dataplane runtime, that repair scales to adversarially poisoned contexts, or that similar repair effects will hold across different models, verifier implementations, or live vendor-specific devices. Those questions require additional experiments (multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate design deliberately isolates repair effects but does not address prompt sensitivity or model-sampling variability; temperature = null/unset in the model configuration is recorded but is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded syntactic and ordering invariants but is not a substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor runtime semantics. External validity: single-model execution (declared gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank limit generality to other models, task families, or production device heterogeneity. Statistical: with only one discordant pair the power to detect small repair-only effects is limited; the archived bootstrap CI quantifies that uncertainty.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini and a deterministic_netops_validator_v5 oracle, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. These archived artifacts support the constrained conclusion that verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic, verifier-backed setting; broader operational claims require further targeted experiments and emulation across models, verifiers, and live-device contexts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
